name: Space Syntax Integration as Inverse Navigational Prediction Error
panel_source: SPATIAL-I (Sprint 13.17) — upgrades SC-I structural YAML (Doc 38) and SC-II partial calibration (Doc 62)

t1_5_parent_theories.name: Space Syntax (Hillier & Hanson, 1984)
t1_5_parent_theories.reduction_pathway: Formally reduced to SN, PP, EC in T1_5_Expansion (Feb 21 Session 5). Space Syntax integration IS a topological measure of path predictability, which IS what the PP framework predicts agents optimize. The reduction is constitutive, not merely analogical.

t1_5_parent_theories.name: Prospect-Refuge Theory (Appleton, 1975)
t1_5_parent_theories.reduction_pathway: Applies at macro-scale: high integration spaces offer a form of 'prospect' (visual and navigational access) while reduced integration characterizes refuge spaces. Partial overlap — Prospect-Refuge operates at isovist scale (→ SC2), but the integration-safety connection shares evolutionary grounding.

mechanism_chain.description: Spatial integration is computed from the topological graph of the building: the mean topological depth from each space to all other spaces. High integration = few turns to reach from everywhere = high navigational predictability.
mechanism_chain.neural_substrate: No direct neural measurement; the environmental property (integration) is the input variable

data.finding: Integration-movement correlation r ≈ 0.72 replicated across hundreds of buildings, cultures, and scales
data.effect: r = 0.72 for integration-pedestrian movement; meta-analytic level evidence
data.design: Cross-sectional observation across hundreds of buildings

data.finding: Integration is a topological measure of mean depth from each space to all others — high integration = few turns to reach everywhere
data.effect: Formal mathematical definition; no effect size per se

justification.backing: The integration-movement correlation is one of the most replicated findings in architectural research. Hundreds of studies across cultures and building types confirm r ≈ 0.60-0.80. Hillier (panel position statement): "the BEHAVIORAL correlation is meta-analytic level evidence." The PE interpretation — that integration operationalizes navigational predictability — is Hillier's theoretical contribution, not directly measured.
justification.qualifier: Step 1 is definitional (environmental → formal_architectural), so confidence is inherent to the measure. The question is whether integration captures what the brain computes. Hillier explicitly distinguishes: "I am claiming that integration measures the property (predictability) that the nervous system optimizes, not that I have measured the neural circuit." The integration metric is a FUNCTIONAL bridge, not a MECHANISM bridge.
justification.rebuttal: The claim would fail if: (a) integration captures path simplicity but the brain does not optimize for this — if navigators use landmarks, signage, or social information rather than topological integration, the metric captures a mathematical property of the plan but not the cognitive variable; (b) the correlation is confounded by other properties that co-vary with integration (ceiling height, daylight, material quality).

mechanism_chain.description: A navigator in a high-integration space can form a reliable spatial ROUTE SCHEMA — the expected turn sequence to reach any destination — using fewer working memory resources than in a low-integration space. The route schema is encoded in working memory via prefrontal-hippocampal networks.
mechanism_chain.neural_substrate: Prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) working memory maintenance; hippocampal CA3-CA1 pattern completion supporting route recall; entorhinal grid cells providing metric scaffold (Meilinger et al., 2008; O'Keefe & Nadel, 1978)

data.finding: Wayfinding uses combination of SURVEY knowledge (map-like) and ROUTE knowledge (turn sequences), both competing for working memory
data.effect: Route complexity predicts working memory load during navigation

data.finding: Low-integration buildings require more turns → harder route knowledge → more working memory load
data.effect: Working memory load inversely proportional to integration

justification.backing: Meilinger supplied the missing cognitive link: Integration → Route complexity → Working memory load → Prefrontal-hippocampal coupling demands → Available cognitive resources → Residual emotional state. The pathway goes through working memory and PFC rather than directly through limbic valutation. Dalton (panel debate) confirmed: stationary r ≈ 0.40 vs navigating r ≈ 0.55, supporting both WM (navigation-amplified) and visual monitoring (present stationary) pathways.
justification.qualifier: Meilinger proposed MECHANISM warrant at confidence 0.60 for the WM pathway. Shahar adjudicated: EMPIRICAL_COVARIANCE for the integration-valence link with WM as "MOST LIKELY mechanism but not confirmed." The dual pathway (WM during navigation + visual monitoring during stationary) is the panel consensus.
justification.rebuttal: Hillier contested Meilinger's primacy for WM: "People SITTING in a high-integration space report more positive affect... even when not navigating. The effect persists when navigational demands are removed." Dalton's data partially resolved this: both pathways operate, WM dominant during navigation, visual monitoring residual when stationary.

competing_accounts.claim: Integration affects valence through direct visual monitoring efficiency, not primarily through WM load — the effect persists for stationary occupants
competing_accounts.implication_for_template: If direct visual pathway, SC1 applies equally to navigating and sedentary occupants. If WM pathway, SC1 effect is amplified during navigation (r=0.55) vs stationary (r=0.40). Panel consensus: both operate, proportions uncertain.

mechanism_chain.description: High-integration paths produce CONFIRMED spatial predictions — the navigator predicts the next junction type and finds it. Confirmed spatial predictions generate a smooth updating of the hippocampal place cell map with low metabolic demand. Low-integration paths generate frequent prediction errors — unexpected junctions, confusing loops — triggering hippocampal prediction error signals and updating demands.
mechanism_chain.neural_substrate: Hippocampal CA1 place cells — mismatch-detection mechanism (Kumaran & Maguire, 2007); dopamine-mediated prediction error from VTA to hippocampus; LC noradrenergic arousal for unexpected navigational events

data.finding: Hippocampal CA1 mismatch-detection mechanism generates PE for unexpected spatial events
data.effect: CA1 activation scales with mismatch magnitude

data.finding: Frontal EEG asymmetry correlates with integration value in VR navigation
data.effect: Greater left frontal activation (approach) in high-integration paths

justification.backing: The neural mechanism (place cell mismatch detection → hippocampal PE signal → VTA dopaminergic modulation) is well established in animal navigation neuroscience. Banaei's VR-EEG study provides the closest human architectural confirmation: frontal asymmetry consistent with approach motivation in high-integration paths. However, Hillier acknowledged: "the full human chain has not been measured in architectural contexts."
justification.qualifier: MECHANISM warrant for the neural pathway but confidence limited by the transfer from animal neuroscience + VR to real architectural contexts. The place-cell-valence hypothesis is "theoretically coherent and supported by analogous animal data, but the full human chain has not been measured in architectural contexts" (Hillier position statement).
justification.rebuttal: The claim would fail if: (a) human place cells in complex buildings do not show the same reliability gradient as in animal studies — the hippocampal mapping of multi-story, multi-function buildings may be qualitatively different from rodent maze navigation; (b) Banaei's EEG effect is driven by visual complexity/openness confounded with integration rather than by integration per se.

mechanism_chain.description: Elevated working memory load during low-integration navigation produces sustained DLPFC activation that competes with task-relevant processes and generates an aversive signal of cognitive effort. This is the primary mechanism for the integration-valence correlation in navigating occupants.
mechanism_chain.neural_substrate: DLPFC (Brodmann 46/9) sustained activation under load; anterior cingulate cortex conflict monitoring at ambiguous junctions; reduced DLPFC availability for non-navigational cognition

data.finding: DLPFC sustained activation under navigational load produces aversive cognitive effort signal
data.paradigm: WM load → prefrontal demand → reduced available cognition
data.effect: DLPFC activation inversely proportional to spatial predictability

data.finding: Integration-valence r = 0.55 drops to r = 0.40-0.45 when controlling for luminance
data.design: Cross-sectional field study with partial correlation

justification.backing: WM load during navigation is the primary mechanism for integration-valence correlation in active navigation. Dalton's partial correlation controlling for luminance (r drops from 0.55 to 0.40-0.45) reveals a significant confound: high-integration buildings tend to have better daylight. Hillier acknowledged this and specified that "Article Eater should apply SC1 only after L-template effects have been accounted for."
justification.qualifier: Confidence 0.55 (panel consensus, Shahar adjudication) with EMPIRICAL_COVARIANCE warrant. The luminance confound reduces the independent integration effect. Order of operations specified: SC1 → L-templates → IC2 → AX4.
justification.rebuttal: The claim would fail if: (a) the luminance confound explains most of the integration-valence correlation, leaving integration with r < 0.30 independent contribution — this would make SC1 practically subordinate to L-templates; (b) the WM load pathway is not aversive per se but only produces negative affect when combined with time pressure or navigational stakes.

mechanism_chain.description: For stationary occupants in high-integration spaces, a secondary mechanism operates: visual co-presence with many sightlines activates the parahippocampal place area (PPA) for scene recognition and provides a continually updated, confident spatial model. This reduces the background monitoring load of the spatial prediction system, contributing to positive valence even without active navigation.
mechanism_chain.neural_substrate: Parahippocampal place area (PPA) scene recognition; reduced lateral prefrontal monitoring demands; lower arousal baseline via LC-NE system; positive affective register via orbitofrontal cortex

data.finding: PPA scene recognition is continuous and automatic for stationary occupants in rich visual scenes
data.effect: PPA responds to scene category automatically

data.finding: Stationary integration-valence correlation r ≈ 0.40 (vs r ≈ 0.55 navigating)

justification.backing: The secondary stationary mechanism operates through PPA-mediated scene monitoring: high-integration spaces provide rich, spatially extended visual input that reduces background spatial uncertainty. Dalton confirmed the residual stationary effect (r ≈ 0.40). This is the visual monitoring pathway Hillier advocated, operating through reduced spatial prediction load rather than WM load.
justification.qualifier: This step represents the portion of SC1 that applies to all occupants, not just navigators. The confidence is lower than the navigating pathway because the mechanism is less directly evidenced. The effect may be partially confounded with other correlates of high-integration spaces (better light, more social life, more amenities).
justification.rebuttal: The claim would fail if: (a) the stationary effect is entirely explained by confounds (light, social density, amenity proximity) that happen to correlate with integration values; (b) PPA scene monitoring does not produce positive valence directly — it provides spatial confidence but this is affectively neutral.

mechanism_chain.description: Integration-valence is partially confounded with luminance: high-integration buildings tend to have better natural light penetration. When luminance is held constant (partial correlation), integration-valence drops from r = 0.55 to r = 0.40–0.45. Article Eater must apply L-template effects before applying SC1 integration effects.
mechanism_chain.neural_substrate: Interaction between spatial and visual processing pathways — the dorsal 'where' stream integrates spatial configuration with luminance cues

data.finding: Integration-valence partial r = 0.40-0.45 controlling for illuminance

justification.backing: This step is a METHODOLOGICAL NOTE, not a mechanism step per se. It establishes the critical constraint that SC1 must be applied AFTER L-template correction to avoid double-counting luminance effects. Meilinger specified the order: SC1 → L-templates → IC2 → AX4.
justification.qualifier: High confidence for the confound identification itself. The partial correlation approach is standard but may not fully control for luminance if the luminance-integration relationship is nonlinear or if luminance distribution matters more than average illuminance.

spatial_configuration.construct: Correlation between building intelligibility (local connectivity-global integration correlation) and wayfinding success rate
spatial_configuration.unit: Pearson r (negative: lower intelligibility → more errors)
source_panels: SC-II: Dalton angular depth data r=0.61 for 'I feel lost' rating; Hölscher et al. (2006) wayfinding error distribution

elderly_65_plus.modifier: +heightened sensitivity — angular depth errors accumulate faster; floor confusion more frequent

age_group.modifier: +heightened sensitivity — developing cognitive map capacity; earlier disorientation in low-intelligibility buildings

spatial_enclosure_ratio.construct: Multiplier for prediction error cost per floor transition beyond single-floor baseline, by transition type
spatial_enclosure_ratio.unit: PE multiplier relative to single-floor baseline
spatial_enclosure_ratio.mechanism: Grid cell anisotropy: hippocampal-entorhinal mapping system codes horizontal position with high precision (small grid cell spacing, sharp place fields) and vertical position with low precision (elongated place fields, disrupted grid symmetry) — Jeffery et al. (2013); Hayman et al. (2011). Floor transitions disrupt the horizontal coordinate system and require reconstruction from non-spatial cues.

atrium_mitigation.source: Hölscher IAPS 2024 field data (N=312, 6 hospitals): 31% reduction; SC-II range 30–50% revised downward to reflect real-building atria with partial obstruction
atrium_mitigation.note: Applies to cross-floor visual atria only; enclosed atria without cross-floor sightlines produce no mitigation

floor_distinctiveness_modifier.source: Hölscher IAPS 2024: 22% → 8% floor confusion rate with visually distinctive floors

ie_dpt_interaction.mechanism: The implicit channel continuously monitors spatial integration cues — available paths, visible exits, co-presence of others — and generates implicit safety estimates. High integration is implicitly associated with spatial control and safety; low integration with spatial entrapment and threat. This implicit evaluation precedes and shapes the explicit wayfinding strategy.
ie_dpt_interaction.explicit_channel: T_IE_003 (Route Planning) — the explicit channel engages deliberately when the implicit spatial safety assessment signals navigational uncertainty above a threshold, triggering deliberate route planning.

primary: Hospitals (high-stakes wayfinding, elderly population, high repeat exposure)
low_applicability: Small single-story residences (single room depth, trivial integration)
Retail environments with deliberate disorientation design (maze-layout strategy reversal)

panel_reasoning_excerpt:
### Panel Discussion: What Does VIEW1 Change in Document 33?

**Reinhart**: VIEW1 is a cross-cutting template. Unlike templates that primarily serve a single domain (L1 → A4, SC1 → A3), VIEW1 engages multiple attribute domains through its five channels.

**A4 Light & Luminance**: VIEW1 connects through Channels 4 (temporal variation → L5) and through the VIEW1-L3 super-additive interaction. The window that delivers a nature view simultaneously delivers daylight. VIEW1 strengthens the case for A4 by specifying that the VIEW function of windows is mechanistically independent of (but convergent with) the light function.

**A6 Visual Pattern & Form**: VIEW1 connects through Channel 1 (fractal fluency → T1). The nature view IS a visual pattern — specifically, the paradigmatic example of the fractal patterns that T1 formalizes. VIEW1 strengthens A6 by establishing that the most effective delivery of fractal visual content is through real nature views rather than artificial fractal patterns.

**A3 Spatial Configuration**: VIEW1 connects through Channel 2 (prospect/spatial depth → SC2). A nature view extends the occupant's effective isovist beyond the room boundary. VIEW1 adds to A3 by formalizing the window as a spatial-configuration element — it modifies the room's perceived spatial extent.

**A9 Task & Cognition**: VIEW1 connects through Channel 3 (attention restoration → T25). Nature views restore directed attention. VIEW1 strengthens the attention sub-domain of A9 by specifying the window as the primary architectural delivery mechanism for attention restoration during sustained task performance.

**Coverage rating impact**: VIEW1 does not change any A-domain's rating because it is a cross-cutting template that reinforces existing coverage rather than filling a gap in any single domain. Its primary contribution is to CONNECT existing domains: A4, A6, A3, and A9 are now linked through the window-as-convergence-device rather than being treated as independent.

IC2_body_budget.interaction: Low integration → sustained navigational PE → elevated prefrontal-hippocampal demand → IC2 allostatic cost accumulation over extended occupancy. The body budget costs of chronic navigational difficulty are greatest in building types with high repeat-visit load: hospitals, schools, offices. Buildings where occupants spend >4 hours/day in low-integration conditions create measurable allostatic load via the IC2 pathway.
IC2_body_budget.direction: SC1 feeds IC2 as upstream trigger

AX4_perceived_control.interaction: Integration modulates AX4 perceived control over spatial environment. High-integration buildings confer the sense that one CAN navigate — that departure and return are reliably achievable. This is perceived spatial agency, and it is one of the primary contributors to AX4 scores in buildings. Low integration produces the specific AX4 failure mode of navigational helplessness — the person knows they cannot efficiently navigate and anticipates failure. This anticipatory loss of control is distinct from the PE of actual disorientation.
AX4_perceived_control.direction: SC1 feeds AX4 as a primary architectural determinant of spatial agency
